rows.name: TEST_FPGA_RESULT

rows.values: Text. The step sets it from the expression `needs.test-fpga.result`, the result of job `test-fpga`. Only the exact text `success` passes.
rows.default: Unset: the `test` command compares an empty text with `success`. The step fails.
rows.effect: The step runs `test "$TEST_FPGA_RESULT" = success`. Any other value fails the step.
rows.notes: The same step checks `BUILD_RESULT` and `TEST_HOST_RESULT` in the same way.

rows.name: TEST_HOST_RESULT
rows.read_by: The step `Require successful dependencies` of job `test` (`.github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml`)

rows.effect: The step runs `test "$TEST_HOST_RESULT" = success`. Any other value fails the step.

rows.name: TEST_RUNTIME_STORE_PATH
rows.values: Path of the test runtime (the Nix build output that the CI test jobs run). After symbolic links are resolved, it must have the form `/nix/store/<32 characters>-<name>`.
rows.default: Unset: `publish_lab.py` stops with a `KeyError`. `prepare_handoff.py` requires the option `--test-runtime`. Empty: both scripts stop with `invalid canonical Nix store path`.
rows.effect: `prepare_handoff.py` writes the resolved path as the output `test_runtime_store_path`. It also checks if the tests of this runtime already passed. `publish_lab.py` passes the path to `nix-instantiate` as the argument `testRuntime`.
rows.notes: A path of another form gives the error `invalid canonical Nix store path`. `publish_lab.py` also requires an existing path. In `prepare_handoff.py`, the option `--test-runtime` overrides the variable. Job `tron-build` sets it for 2 steps: first to the build result link, then to the handoff output.

rows.name: TIMEOUT_OVERRIDE
rows.read_by: The step `Validate refresh invocation` of job `plan` (`.github/workflows/bench-refresh.yml`)
rows.values: Empty, or digits only: a whole number from `60` to `5400` seconds. Job `plan` takes it from the workflow input `measurement_timeout_seconds`. The input default is empty.
rows.default: Unset: `bench-refresh-ci.sh validate-invocation` receives an empty argument. It skips the timeout check.
rows.effect: The step passes the value to `bench-refresh-ci.sh validate-invocation`. A non-empty value passes only when the event is `workflow_dispatch` and the dry-run state is `true`. A value outside the range fails the step.
rows.notes: This variable only validates the input. Job `refresh` reads the same input as `SLICE_REFRESH_MEASUREMENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`. That variable sets the timeout of the Slice cost measurement. Both error texts start with `measurement timeout override`.

evidence.quote: echo "measurement timeout override must be between 60 and 5400 seconds" \
echo "measurement timeout override requires a dispatched dry run" >&2

rows.name: TRON_BENCHMARK_CACHE_ROOT
rows.who_sets: `bin/ci/tron-build/test_benchmark_runtime.py`, for a test. No workflow sets it.
rows.values: Absolute path of a directory. The helper `ci-shared-nfs.sh ensure-dir` rejects a relative path and a symbolic link. It creates a missing directory and sets the mode to `777`.
rows.effect: `run_benchmark.sh` (the CI benchmark script) keeps each result here as `benchmark.<result identity>.json`. When that regular file exists, the script copies it to the result path. It does not measure again.
rows.notes: The option `--force` removes the cached file and measures again. Job `benchmark` passes `--force` on the second and later run attempts. The result identity is a SHA-256 hash of the payload identity, the source hash, the machine class and the host identity.

rows.name: TRON_BENCHMARK_ENVIRONMENT
rows.who_sets: `bin/ci/tron-build/benchmark_runtime.py`, and `bin/ci/tron-build/test_benchmark_runtime.py` for a test. The `prepare` command of `benchmark_runtime.py` appends the variable to the `GITHUB_ENV` file (the file that sets variables for the later steps of a job).
rows.read_by: `run_benchmark.sh` (`bin/ci/tron-build/run_benchmark.sh`). The step `Install torch export dependencies` of job `benchmark` (`.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`).
rows.values: Path of the benchmark environment (the Nix store path that holds the benchmark tools `bin/uv` and `bin/python3`). The readers use the text as given.

rows.name: TRON_BENCHMARK_HOST_IDENTITY
rows.who_sets: `bin/ci/tron-build/test_benchmark_runtime.py`, for a test. No workflow sets it.
rows.values: Any non-empty text. The script uses it in a file name and as one input of a hash. A new measurement succeeds only when the text equals the host name.
rows.default: Unset: the output of the `hostname` command.
rows.effect: `run_benchmark.sh` names the result file `<git sha7>.<host identity>.json`. The text is also one input of the result identity (the hash that names the cached result file).

After a measurement, `run_benchmark.sh` copies `<git sha7>.<host identity>.json` to the cache. With a value that differs from the host name, this copy finds no file and the script fails.

evidence.quote: shard_id = socket.gethostname()  # one shard per machine

rows.name: TRON_MODEL_CACHE_LEASE_FDS

new_terms.definition: A file that GitHub Actions gives to each job. A step writes a line `NAME=value` to it. The later steps of the same job then have that variable in their environment.
The Nix build output that the CI test jobs run. It is one Nix store path. It holds the `gen/` tree and the file `gen/ci-test-manifest.json`.
The Nix store path that holds the tools of the CI test jobs: `bin/uv`, `bin/python3`, `bin/tron-test-host`, `bin/tron-test-fpga` and the directory `lib`.
The Nix build output that the CI benchmark job runs. It is one Nix store path. It holds `gen/runtron` and the manifest `gen/ci-benchmark-manifest.json`.
The Nix store path that holds the tools of the CI benchmark job: `bin/uv` and `bin/python3`.
The script `bin/ci/tron-build/run_benchmark.sh`. It runs the CI benchmarks with the prepared benchmark runtime, or it reuses a cached result.
The SHA-256 hash of the benchmark runtime path and the benchmark environment path. It has 64 hexadecimal characters.
The SHA-256 hash of the payload identity, the source hash, the machine class and the host identity. `run_benchmark.sh` names the cached result file with it.

7 hexadecimal characters that identify the tracked source files. The workflows compute them with `git ls-files` and `sha256sum`. The test artifact scripts take the source hash as their first argument `<sha7>`.

The empty file `<root>/<source hash>/nix-tests-<identity>.passed`. `test_runtime.py mark-passed` creates it after the tests of one test runtime and one test environment pass. `<identity>` is a SHA-256 hash of the 2 store paths.
The Torch traces of the selected models, in one bundle. The job `build-model-traces` of `.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml` builds them with `nix/model-traces-entry.nix`.

An open file descriptor that holds a shared lock on one lock file of the CI model weights cache. The lock files are under `state/locks` in the weights root. The cache cleanup takes the same lock exclusively.
A path of the form `/nix/store/<32 characters>-<name>`. It names one Nix output.
The name of one type of benchmark runner, for example `2x96core`. Job `benchmark` of `.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml` passes it to `run_benchmark.sh` as the fourth argument.
The text that names the machine in a benchmark result file. `run_benchmark.sh` takes it from `TRON_BENCHMARK_HOST_IDENTITY`, or from the `hostname` command.
The first 7 characters of the Git commit hash that the benchmark job checked out. It is the third argument of `run_benchmark.sh`.

notes: Short version: 18 rows, one per input variable, no row dropped. 13 rows changed. 5 rows are unchanged: TEST_FPGA_RESULT, TEST_HOST_RESULT, TRACE_INPUTS, TRON_BENCHMARK_PAYLOAD_IDENTITY and TRON_BENCHMARK_PYTHON. In TRON_BENCHMARK_ENVIRONMENT only the wording changed. All 66 evidence quotes of the writer matched the checkout. The writer note counts 67. A count over the rows file gives 66. Two cells named a file that does not contain the variable name. TIMEOUT_OVERRIDE `read_by` named `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh`. TOOLCHAIN_RESULT `who_sets` named `bin/ci/test_build_test_stage.py`. Both are fixed. Source choices confirmed. The 5 variables that a step writes to the GITHUB_ENV file keep `step env`. The rows JOB_TEMP, SOURCE_HASH and SOURCE_SHA of the other ci chunks use the same choice. TIMEOUT_OVERRIDE keeps `workflow env`, like the other job-level entries of job `plan`. TRON_BUILD_ARTIFACT_ROOT keeps `workflow env`. Its `who_sets` cell now says that no other workflow sets it. TRON_MODEL_CACHE_LEASE_FDS keeps `script`. Facts that are new in this pass. TRON_BENCHMARK_HOST_IDENTITY: a value that differs from the host name makes `run_benchmark.sh` fail after a real measurement. TRON_BUILD_ARTIFACT_ROOT: the value must be absolute for the scripts that write, the cleanup script deletes old directories under the value that the workflow passes, and `.github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml` writes one literal `/scratch/tron-build` path. TEST_RUNTIME_STORE_PATH: an empty value fails with a different error than an unset one. 3 statements rest on GitHub Actions or shell behaviour and not on code in the checkout. First, a variable in the GITHUB_ENV file reaches the later steps of the job. Second, an unset variable expands to an empty text in a `run:` script (default cells of TRACE_INPUTS, TIMEOUT_OVERRIDE, TRON_BUILD_STORE_PATH, TRON_TEST_ENVIRONMENT, UV_VERSION). Third, the expression `env.NAME` gives an empty text for a name that is not defined (default cell of TRON_BENCHMARK_RUNTIME_LIBRARY_PATH). Word limits leave no room to define every term inside each cell. The terms `source hash`, `payload identity`, `machine class`, `host identity` and `git sha7` are defined in `new_terms` only. The term `marker of passed tests` is defined in the TRON_BUILD_ARTIFACT_ROOT row and in `new_terms`.
